doc.title: James Hunter interviewed by Monk Rowe, Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Set lists and recording to eight-track at Daptone
summary: Hunter says the set list is fixed for the tour, and discusses Daptone and Gabe Roth's analog approach.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yes indeed. When you write your set list for tonight what goes into that?
Same stuff we’ve been doing the whole tour. Yeah, we’ve got it printed out. Yeah I don’t tailor it around, you know, we stick to one and just get used to the shape of it Yeah.
Sometimes I mean we’ve got enough stuff, you know, but I don’t move it around very often you know. I might change it for the next tour.
And you recorded — sometimes you record straight to eight track?
Well they always do that. Well not really it’s been done to death in the old days hasn’t it.
It’s just that very few people are doing it now.
Yeah. People tend to get — when they have all this gear they can use you feel like you want to use it.

Yeah. Well in Gabe’s case, Gabe Roth, he says you can do anything on digital that you can do on analog, he just prefers the process. He just enjoys it more, you know, the editing and everything. He says you can get all the effects and sounds. His whole thing is mic placement, you know, where you put the mic and what mic to use. That’s how you get the sound.
